questions.solution:

For, (33, 198, 22)

⇒ 42 × 6 = 252. (Second number is 254, 254 ≠ 252)

Here, logic not followed.

⇒ 42 × 6 = 252 ≠ 26 × 9 = 234

Here, logic not followed.

**Option 3) (40, 252, 28)**

⇒ First number multiply by 6: 40 × 6 = 240. (Second number is 252, 252 ≠ 240)

Here, logic not followed.

**Option 4) (42, 252, 28)**

⇒ 42 × 6 = 252 = 28 × 9

**Here, logic followed.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question:
A question is given, followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements is sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and select the appropriate answer.

**Question: **Six people sit in two parallel rows. In Row 1 - J, K and L sit facing towards north, and in Row 2 - F, G and H sit facing towards south. Each person in a row faces a person in the other row. Who faces G?

**Statements:**

(I) H faces K; L faces an immediate neighbour of H.

(II) G sits at one of the extreme ends of the row; J sits to the immediate left of L.

options.text: Data in statements I and II together is sufficient to answer the question
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not
Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not
Data in either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
**Given : **

 
• Six people sit in two parallel rows. 
 
• In Row 1 - J, K and L sit facing towards north. 
 
• In Row 2 - F, G and H sit facing towards south. 
 
• Each person in a row faces a person in the other row.

**Explanation : **

 
• **Statement (I) → **H faces K; L faces an immediate neighbor of H.

​As any specific position of H, L and K cannot be determined, so no specific answer can drawn from it as this statement gives many possibilities.

**So, statement (I) is not sufficient to answer the question.**

 
• Statement (II) → G sits at one of the extreme ends of the row; J sits to the immediate left of L.​

​As any specific position of G, J and L cannot be determined, so no specific answer can drawn from it as this statement gives many possibilities.

**So, statement (II) is not sufficient to answer the question.**

Now, Using both the statements :

 
• Statement (I) + Statement (II) → H faces K; L faces an immediate neighbor of H. ​G sits at one of the extreme ends of the row; J sits to the immediate left of L.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7346bb6f2792cbe41fbc3e52605d6203771f08d72b8ed7ffa0c4641422240935.png] ​

**So, using both the statements, J faces G. Thus data in statements I and II together is sufficient to answer the question.**

Hence, **"Option - (1)"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 53 × 61 × 9 = 123 and 34 × 43 × 24 = 101, then 41 × 16 × 71 = ?

Here sign “×“ denotes the addition i.e.

Similarly,

41 × 16 × 71 → 41 + 16 + 71 = 128.

Hence, 128 is the correct option.

questions.question:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10
questions.solution:
Here, we use the table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e5eadb7fb717e58fc4d0289a0ba8a184fd97b6cf1ef93972c2170c66d3e1984.png] 

Given equations:

⇒ 84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10

Checking all the given options:

**(1) 6 and 14**

⇒ 84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10

After interchanging:

⇒ __**84 ÷ 14**__ + 16 - 6 × 2 = 10

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 6 + 16 - __**6 × 2**__

⇒ __**6 + 16**__ - 12

⇒ 22 - 12 = **10**

⇒ '84 ÷ 14 + 16 - 6 × 2 = 10'

Here, the equation is** satisfied.**

**(2) 2 and 84**

⇒ 84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10

After interchanging:

⇒ __**2 ÷ 6**__ + 16 - 14 × 84 = 10

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 0.33 + 16 - __**14 × 84**__

⇒ 0.33 + 16 - 1176

⇒ (-1159.67)

⇒ '2 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 84 = (-1159.67)'

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

**(3) 10 and 14**

⇒ 84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10

After interchanging:

⇒ __**84 ÷ 6**__ + 16 - 10 × 2 = 14

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 14 + 16 - __**10 × 2**__

⇒ __**14 + 16**__ - 20

⇒ 30 - 20 = 10

⇒ '84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 10 × 2 = 10'

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

**(4) 6 and 10**

⇒ 84 ÷ 6 + 16 - 14 × 2 = 10

After interchanging:

⇒ __**84 ÷ 10**__ + 16 - 14 × 2 = 6

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 8.4 + 16 - __**14 × 2**__

⇒ __**8.4 + 16**__ - 28

⇒ 24.4 - 28 = (-3.6)

⇒ '84 ÷ 10 + 16 - 14 × 2 = (-3.6)'

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (1)".

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(15, 14, 13)

(12, 10, 8)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: The second number in the set is the arithmetic mean (average) of the first and the third numbers.**

**i.e., N₂ = (N₁ + N₃) / 2**

Let's check the given sets based on this logic:

**For (15, 14, 13):**

→ N₁ = 15, N₃ = 13

→ (15 + 13) / 2 = 28 / 2 = 14

→ The second number is 14. (Matches)

**For (12, 10, 8):**

→ N₁ = 12, N₃ = 8

→ (12 + 8) / 2 = 20 / 2 = 10

→ The second number is 10. (Matches)

Now, let's apply this logic to the given options:

**Option 1) (11, 22, 12)**

→ N₁ = 11, N₃ = 12

→ (11 + 12) / 2 = 23 / 2 = 11.5

→ Since 11.5 ≠ 22,

This option does not follow the logic.

**Option 2) (10, 12, 8)**

→ N₁ = 10, N₃ = 8

→ (10 + 8) / 2 = 18 / 2 = 9

→ Since 9 ≠ 12,

This option does not follow the logic.

**Option 3) (15, 15, 15)**

→ N₁ = 15, N₃ = 15

→ (15 + 15) / 2 = 30 / 2 = 15

**→ Since 15 = 15,**

**This option follows the logic.**

**Option 4) (13, 11, 7)**

→ N₁ = 13, N₃ = 7

→ (13 + 7) / 2 = 20 / 2 = 10

→ Since 10 ≠ 11,

This option does not follow the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
Direction : In the following questions, a statement followed by two conclusions is given. Read the statements carefully and decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s).

Statement : Parents are prepared to pay any price for an elite education of their children.

Conclusions :

I. All parents these days are very well off.

II. Parents have an obsessive passion for perfect development of their children through good schooling.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
Given:

Statement : Parents are prepared to pay any price for an elite education of their children.

The statement says that nowadays parents are forever ready to pay any price, no matter how big or small it is, just for the proper quality education for their kids.

Conclusion I does not follow as there is no clue regarding the parents' financial soundness. Instead of “All”, if “Some” was used, conclusion I would have followed as well.

Conclusion II says that parents try to provide perfect and wholesome development for their kids through quality education by enrolling them into good schools. It means that parents are driven by a desire. Hence “any price” can be linked with “obsessive passion”.

Thus, conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2."**
